messages.author: 55e546e375e22a40
messages.subject: correction for multiple testing
parts:
Hi,
Does anyone know how to correct for multiple testing in R/qtl or elsewhere for several phenotypes. Currently, the permutation testing in R/qtl corrects for genome wide QTL testing for each phenotype. But say I have several phenotypes, as in eQTL mapping, how do I correct for the testing of several phenotypes? Previously, R/qtl did not have any feature to do this, other than permutation testing which correct for QTL scans at several markers, I don't know if this has changed or not.
Thanks.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] correction for multiple testing
parts:
If it's two or three phenotypes, I wouldn't correct for the multiple phenotypes.

If it's 10-20, I would control the family-wise error rate (FWER). See Burrage et al. Mamm Genome 21:115-129, 2010

http://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/burrage.pdf

If it's >1,000 traits, I would either (1) don't control but be direct about what you did and about the chance of false positives, or (2) seek to control FDR across phenotypes (but still control the FWER for the scan across the genome).

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] correction for multiple testing
parts:
The simplest approach is to use a common threshold for all phenotypes.

Then be sure that the permutations for the different phenotypes are conducted together in scanone, so that any correlations among phenotypes is preserved in the permutations:

perms <- scanone(mycross, pheno.col = 1:nphe(mycross), n.perm=1000)

Then you just take the maximum across phenotypes:

maxperms <- apply(perms, 1, max)

and then the quantile of this is your threshold:

threshold <- quantile(maxperms, 0.95)

karl
